description: We're a team of students and tech enthusiasts participating in NASA Space Apps 2026! Our project, SYNORA, is an astronaut health-monitoring platform designed for long-duration space missions. Using AI-assisted development, we're combining health data visualization, intelligent monitoring, and interactive pixel-art companions controlled through gestures and voice commands. We're passionate about building creative, and meaningful technology.
summary:
SYNORA is an offline capable health companion designed for astronauts on long missions helping them understand and manage their well-being. It tracks vital signs, sleep, mood, stress, and radiation exposure, helping astronauts recognize concerning health trends and understand what actions they can take.

To address the challenge, SYNORA combines interactive health visualizations, trend tracking, a simulated 180-day mission, and a customizable pixel-art companion that encourages consistent monitoring through rewards and interactive controls.

SYNORA aims to help astronauts recognize potential health concerns, maintain healthy routines, and make informed decisions when immediate medical assistance from Earth is unavailable.
details:
SYNORA is a web-based health monitoring application we developed to help astronauts take care of their physical and mental well-being during long-duration space missions. It allows astronauts to track vital signs, sleep, stress, mood, and radiation exposure, while providing clear health assessments and practical guidance. We also included interactive health charts, a body overview, and a 180-day Mars mission simulator to show how health conditions can change over time.

One thing we wanted to focus on was the human side of space travel. Astronauts spend long periods away from family, friends, and the everyday comforts of Earth. That's why we added a customizable pixel-art companion that responds to their well-being and can be interacted with through hand gestures, voice commands, and simple activities. We wanted health monitoring to feel less like a chore and more like something astronauts would actually look forward to using.

We built SYNORA using React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Recharts, IndexedDB, and MediaPipe, with assistance from Claude Code. Throughout development, we focused on keeping the application easy to use, privacy-conscious, and functional without an internet connection. We also used research from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency to guide our understanding of space-related health challenges.

Our goal with SYNORA is to give astronauts a little more independence when medical support from Earth isn't immediately available, while making their daily health routines easier, more engaging, and a little more personal. It's an early prototype, but we hope it can serve as a foundation for more advanced astronaut health monitoring tools in the future.
